events.title: Francis Drake Completes His Circumnavigation
events.description: Sir Francis Drake brought the Golden Hind into Plymouth Harbour. The voyage had taken nearly three years. It was the second circumnavigation of the globe, and the first led by a single commander throughout.
events.significance: The voyage made Drake a national hero and brought his backers a huge fortune in captured Spanish treasure. It also helped establish England as a rising maritime power.

events.title: The Parthenon Is Shattered by an Explosion
events.description: During the Venetian siege of Athens, a Venetian bombardment hit Ottoman forces' gunpowder store inside the Parthenon. The blast tore apart the roof and much of the building. It had survived largely intact for over two thousand years.
events.significance: The damage is still visible today. The event also fed later debates about protecting cultural heritage during war.

events.title: The First Televised US Presidential Debate
events.description: John F. Kennedy and Richard Nixon met in a Chicago studio before an audience of tens of millions of viewers. It was the first televised debate between US presidential candidates.
events.significance: The debate showed how much image and presentation could matter on television, and it changed how political campaigns are run.

events.title: Stanislav Petrov Questions a False Missile Alert
events.description: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov was on duty at an early-warning command center when its system reported incoming US missiles. He judged the alarm to be a malfunction and did not pass it up the chain of command as an attack.
events.significance: His decision may have helped prevent a nuclear escalation at a very tense point in the Cold War. It is often cited as an example of human judgment checking automated systems.
